messages:
mira: quick thread  question about pin lifecycle for tenant-scoped canaries. should canary-created pins use shorter TTLs by default?

toni: short answer: yes, but need explicit promotion API so stable rollouts can take over without capacity gaps.

alex: agree. proposal: rollout manifest adds `pin_origin` (canary|stable|manual), `pin_ttl_hint` (secs, advisory), and `pin_intent_id` (uuid) to make resolution deterministic.

sam: also we need a way to label which tenants/shards get the canary. current `cohort` string is too opaque. propose `shard_labels` as list of k=v strings (server canonicalized).

mira: example: {variant:"v2.4-canary",pin_origin:"canary",pin_ttl_hint:"1800",pin_intent_id:"uuid-1234",shard_labels:["region=eu","tier=premium"],promote_token:null}

alex: add `pin_promoted_by` and `pin_promotion_ts` to manifest when promoted for auditing. include `schema_version` so control plane can do graceful migration.

sam: runtime safety: default cap so canary pins can't own >X% of tenant capacity. manifest can include `capacity_override` but requires an approval flag.

deploy-bot: we will emit `pin_expired` events to ops stream (payload: variant,tenant_id,shard_labels,expiry_ts). opening event-schema PR.

toni: i'll draft a short RFC covering fields, label canonicalization rules (sort keys, namespace whitelist), probe API (GET /pins?tenant=&variant=) and migration notes.

mira: i'll review RFC and add telemetry queries to check canary churn and expiry->promotion deltas. closing this thread.
